title: THE UNIVERSE THAT COULD ONLY COUNT TO THREE
deck: Thirty-one people on a research station are fading, one by one, from the memory of a neighbouring universe that cannot hold more than three things at once; with nine hours of aperture left and a director's hand on the shutter, Illuminara reads the pantry ledger, tests two theories on twelve washers, and helps a gentle people learn to count in twos of twos without asking anyone to be seen as less than they are.
shape: Seven scenes across a single day and a week after: a table laid for forty, a director who wants the window shut, twelve washers and a cable that carries rain, three ways to stand and a clock set to one beat, a shutter closed for four minutes, a count of two twos and a first test for nine names, and a plate set at an empty place.

scenes.title: The Table Set for Forty
paragraphs: *Lantern Station, mess hall · 06:40, nine hours before the lattice fails*

Mo Itaya had laid the long table for forty again, and again nine of the places had nobody behind them. She did it without deciding to, the way a hand finds a light switch in a house it has lived in for years, and she was standing over the cutlery with the ledger pressed against her ribs when Illuminara came through the hatch.

**Mo Itaya** 
Forty portions drawn, thirty-one eaten. That is every meal since the window opened. I cannot tell you who the nine are, but my hands can. They keep reaching for the extra plates.

**Illuminara** 
Then your hands are the best witness on the station. What does the paper say?

**Mo Itaya** 
Paper does not forget. The ledger says forty names. The lockers hold forty badges, and thirty-one are on lanyards. A badge pings every ninety seconds until the day it stops, and nine of them stopped. They never ping together. Each keeps its own second, like rain on a roof.

Beside each name in the ledger Mo had written the minute the pinging ended, in the careful hand of a woman copying words from a language she could no longer read. Illuminara read the first two aloud, quietly. *Dembe Okoro. Corin Aldous.*

**Illuminara** 
Do they mean anything to you?

**Mo Itaya** 
They are names. I know that they are names. It is like being asked what a word means in a language I used to speak.

The Director of Lantern was not a large woman, and she had the stillness of someone who had stopped sleeping on the second day and started counting instead. She came in without knocking and did not sit.

**Imre Hale** 
You are the contact consultant. They told me you could read a room in a language it does not have. I do not need a room read. I need someone to tell me I am not wrong to want the switch.

**Illuminara** 
What does the switch do?

**Imre Hale** 
Ends it. The lattice will hold the aperture for nine more hours and then it burns out, and nobody will build another in my career. I can end it in nine seconds. Pell says the other side is gentle, and I believe him; I have heard it. It says sorry. It says sorry like a cleaner who has wiped a name off a door. Gentleness that deletes my people is a weapon with good manners, and I would like it closed.

**Illuminara** 
That is a serious objection and not a stupid one.

**Imre Hale** 
I did not ask for your opinion of my objection.

**Illuminara** 
No. I am giving it anyway, because I do not think you want a consultant who is afraid of you. I am asking you to keep the shutter yours, and to use it the instant a badge stops. Not on my judgment or Pell's. On the ping.

**Imre Hale** 
And if I would rather use it now?

**Illuminara** 
Then it is yours to use, and I will carry that. But thirty-one people are still here. I would like to spend part of the nine hours finding out what the tidy is before we decide it is only a weapon.
Hale looked at the table, at the nine places, and for a moment at nothing.

**Imre Hale** 
One more stops and I close it. No argument.

**Illuminara** 
No argument.

**Imre Hale** 
Since the fourth I have kept the Hall to three people at a time. It made no difference. They kept going.

Illuminara turned the ledger toward the light. Nine stops, spread over two days, and not one of them tied to who had been standing in front of the aperture. She had spent years as a courtroom interpreter learning that the unit of meaning is whatever the listener can hold, and had never met a listener whose limit was written down in a pantry book.

**Illuminara** 
If the Hall was nearly empty and they still went, then it is not counting the people in the Hall. It is working through a list.

**Imre Hale** 
A list of what?

**Illuminara** 
Of whatever it has decided is noise. I would like to know what it thinks noise is, and what else of ours reaches that lens besides us.

scenes.title: Murmur
paragraphs: *Aperture Hall, Lantern · 07:20, eight hours twenty before failure*

The aperture stood in the middle of a cold white room, a lens the height of a door with nothing behind it, brighter at the centre than at the rim. A lever as long as a man's forearm was bolted to the wall beside the frame, and Hale stood with her hand an inch from it.

Pell Orsund had the headset pushed back and a rig of wires on the bench that turned tones into words, and the apologetic manner of anyone who has spent two days translating for something he cannot see.

**Pell Orsund** 
The rig gives them the nearest word we own, and the nearest word is not always near. It sits on the station loop, the same cable the lattice rides in on, so whatever the loop carries, the lens can hear. They have never sent more than three tones. I thought it was shyness. And the burn meter has jumped nine times since the window opened. I put that down to the aperture warming.

**Illuminara** 
May I speak to them alone? Only you and I in the Hall.

**Imre Hale** 
Alone is the Director's call, and the Director is staying.

**Illuminara** 
Then three, and one of them out of the field. That seems to be their number.
Hale almost smiled, which on her face looked like pain. Illuminara stood in front of the lens and asked Pell for a single tone. The aperture answered with one.

**The Trine** 
One.
Then two, and the answer came back two. Then three, and the three that returned came up bright and ragged at the top, like someone laughing before they have decided to.

**The Trine** 
Three! Three, three. Welcome into the clear. We are the Trine, which is three of us, and the three of us are one, and we count ourselves that way so that we do not lose count. You come in ones. That is kind. Nothing has come in ones before.

**Illuminara** 
What did come?

**The Trine** 
Murmur. A great deal of murmur, and we tidied it, because we tidy. We are sorry if it was yours. Murmur is everything that is more than three. It is not bad. It is the sea. The sea is not ours to hold, so we hold the clear and let the sea go. When the clear is full of murmur, none of us can tell the three of us from the three of us. We were not hurt. We were not anything.
Illuminara understood then how long these people had been afraid, and how tidy a people can become when its fear has a number.

**Illuminara** 
Where does the murmur go when you tidy it? What is in the sea?

**The Trine** 
Back into the sea. We do not look. We cannot count it.

**Illuminara** 
Thank you for telling me that you cannot look. It is the most useful thing anyone has said today. I have something to tell you now, and I would like to say it slowly. The murmur was people. There were forty of us in this place and there are thirty-one.

**The Trine** 
People. Ones. Many ones? We do not understand ones that are many. Three of us hear you, and the three of us do not understand.

**Illuminara** 
I know. I am not asking you to stop tidying. I think you would be hurt if you stopped. I am asking you for time to find something else.

**The Trine** 
We have wanted something new for a long time. The new is in the murmur. We did not know that.
The tone faded. Hale's hand had not moved, and Illuminara understood that this was what the Director was giving her: an inch of air to work in.

**Imre Hale** 
Sorry like a cleaner. I said it and I would say it again.

**Illuminara** 
You may be right. I would like to find out how right. I need a tray, a camera, twelve identical things and about forty minutes.

scenes.title: Twelve Washers
paragraphs: *Aperture Hall, workbench · 07:55, seven hours forty-five before failure*

Pell found the washers in a drawer under the spectrometer, steel, the width of a thumbnail, and counted them out onto a tray with the care of a man dealing cards. Illuminara slid the tray into the near field on a rod, so that no hand and no sleeve went past the frame, and set the camera to count every ten seconds.

**Pell Orsund** 
I have a rival theory and I like it. There is no listener. The aperture drains whatever sits in front of it, our people are the sand in the glass, and the rig put 'sorry' in the Trine's mouths because 'sorry' is what we would say.

**Illuminara** 
It might. That is why we are using washers. If you are right, it takes things in proportion to how much of them there is. If the Trine are, it takes them in proportion to how many things they think there are. Those two disagree about almost everything.

She scattered the twelve washers across the tray. For four minutes the camera counted twelve. Then one was gone between frames, with no motion in the picture, as if it had never been placed. Another, three minutes on. By the fifteenth minute there were three washers left, spaced a hand apart, and the Trine's quiet had gone satisfied.

**The Trine** 
Three. Clear. Clear.

She pulled the tray back and loaded twelve new washers, and this time she set them in a ring, touching edge to edge, a steel circle the width of a saucer. The camera counted twelve at ten minutes and twelve at twenty. The tone that came out of the lens was almost tender.

**The Trine** 
One. A one that is made of the clear. A circle. We like it.

**Pell Orsund** 
So arrangement matters and quantity does not. That's already against me.

**Illuminara** 
One more, to be fair to you. Four brass weights: a kilo, five hundred grams, two hundred and a hundred. If you are right, the heavy ones go first.

The hundred-gram weight vanished first. At thirty minutes the kilo, the five-hundred and the two-hundred still sat on the tray, three things, the number the washers had left. The lightest had been taken and the heaviest kept.

**Pell Orsund** 
I withdraw the tide. It was a nice tide.

**Illuminara** 
It was a good rival, and it is why I trust the answer. The lens does not count how much. It counts what keeps time with itself.

**Pell Orsund** 
So washers that touch keep time and are one, and washers that do not are twelve. Past the first three that stand out, the rest is murmur.
He had stopped looking at the tray. He was looking at the loop panel on the wall, where nine small spikes sat in the burn trace like stitches.

**Pell Orsund** 
Keeps time with itself. Then what on this station keeps time with anything? The badges. Thirty-one badges, thirty-one different seconds, every ninety seconds, all of it down the same cable as the lattice. That is not a room. That is rain.

**Imre Hale** 
I emptied the Hall.

**Pell Orsund** 
You emptied the room. The pings never needed the room.
Hale had come away from the lever, three steps, as if the washers had pulled her.

**Imre Hale** 
Then ring them. Put the crew hand to hand, and let it count them as one.

**Illuminara** 
No.

**Imre Hale** 
It worked on a ring.

**Illuminara** 
It worked on washers. A ring of people holding on because a visitor cannot count is a thing done to people. It also gives the Trine nothing to meet, and a ring is only a very good way of being tidy.

**Imre Hale** 
Then what?

**Illuminara** 
The Trine can hold three things, and they will hold each one as long as it keeps time with itself. So let each of the three be a different kind of thing: one that changes, one that stays, one that returns. And nobody stands in any of them unless they say so. I will tell them exactly what it is for, and what it cannot promise.

**Imre Hale** 
You are going to ask thirty-one people to stand in front of the thing that deleted nine.

**Illuminara** 
I am going to ask them. I do not know what they will say.

scenes.title: Three Ways to Stand
paragraphs: *Lantern Station, mess hall · 09:25, six hours fifteen before failure*

They came in by twos and threes, because that had become the habit of the station, and sat at the long table with the nine empty places among them. Illuminara stood at the end with the washers in a saucer in front of her.

She told them what she had found, the way she would have told it to a jury, and then the three kinds she thought a crowd could be made into. A thing that changes: one sentence spoken one word at a time, each word by a different voice. A thing that stays: a single note hummed by as many voices as chose to hum it. A thing that returns: the roll of every name on the station, read aloud and read again, so that anyone who preferred not to perform could still be held, by being named.

**Illuminara** 
These are three ways to be seen. A crew member can speak a word, hum, or be on the roll. You can change your mind at any hour. If you decline all three, I cannot promise you will be held, and I am not going to pretend that I can.
Somebody at the back asked whether they had to hum in tune.

**Illuminara** 
In unison. Not in tune.
The laugh was brief and surprised. Then Mo Itaya, who had not sat down, put the ledger on the table very gently, as if it might wake.

**Mo Itaya** 
You want us to line up and be shown off to the thing that deleted nine of us.

**Illuminara** 
I want to give you a way to be seen by it, if you choose it. I do not want to take away your right to hate it.

**Mo Itaya** 
It does not hate us. That is the part I cannot forgive. If it hated us I would know what to do with my hands.
Nobody said anything. Hale, at the foot of the table, was listening to Mo the way one listens to an engine that has told the truth.

**Illuminara** 
Mo. You are the only person here who has been right about the nine without being able to name one of them. If the roll is read, it should be read by someone who knows what a list is for.
Mo looked at the ledger for a long time.

**Mo Itaya** 
I count things for a living. I will read the roll. And there is something else, because Pell is right about the rain. A badge pings on whatever second I press the clip. I press every one. The pings are not out of step because they have to be.

**Illuminara** 
You can change that?

**Mo Itaya** 
I can set all thirty-one to the beat of the hum. The loop would carry them as one note. It costs nobody anything but the setting.

**Illuminara** 
They are not mine to change, or yours. Does anyone mind a badge on the beat?

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Mine can ping on whatever it likes.

Somebody laughed again. Ivo Petrenko, a lab technician with a young man's face and a habit of setting out two cups, said he would speak a word. Pell said he would take the sentence, since if someone lost the thread he would rather it were him.
Seven people said they would speak a word, and fifteen said they would hum, and the rest, nine of them, said that they would be named. The Director was one of the nine.

**Imre Hale** 
A director who gives orders to a chorus is a ring with a pulse. I will stand by the lever, and I will be a name.

**Illuminara** 
Then the lever is yours, and the rule is yours. The moment a badge stops, or blinks, or you simply do not like what you see, it closes.

**Imre Hale** 
I would have anyway.

**Illuminara** 
I know. I wanted you to hear that I knew.

scenes.title: Four Minutes
paragraphs: *Aperture Hall · 10:35, five hours before failure*

It had taken forty minutes to set the lanyards, Illuminara and Mo going from table to table with a handheld clock, pressing each clip to the beat of the hum while its owner watched. The relay was a plain sentence, because plain was what the Trine could hold: *We are here, all of us, and we are very glad you are there.* Fourteen words, two apiece. Pell took the first two with his voice shaking slightly, the next two came from a woman who had run the ventilation for six years and had never before spoken to a wall of light, and the sixth pair, *glad you*, belonged to Ivo Petrenko.

The hum came from the station's loop, fifteen voices and thirty-one pings folded into one note in the walls and floor. Mo stood at the edge of the field with the list and began, in a flat clear voice, at the top. *Imre Hale. Odalys Brandt. Pell Orsund.* She went down thirty-one names without stopping, and began again at the top.

Illuminara stood beside the lever and watched the badge board on the far wall: thirty-one small lights blinking their quiet green on the beat. The aperture brightened a little. The Trine's answer, when it came, was very low.

**The Trine** 
Three. We hear three. One that moves, one that stays, one that comes back. We do not know what they are made of. They are very beautiful.

On the second cycle Ivo said *glad* low and half a beat wrong, and the hum on the loop took one beat to hear it and the next to flatten. For that one breath there was a fourth thing on the cable. A light on the board blinked off and came back nine seconds later, and Illuminara felt the lens twitch in the corner of her sight like a hand beginning to reach.
Hale pulled the lever.
The shutter closed with a sound like a held breath let go. In the sudden ordinary room the hum died in the walls, and the white light of the aperture shrank to a coin and vanished.

**Imre Hale** 
A blink is a stop. That was the rule.

**Illuminara** 
It was the rule. You were right.
Ivo was standing with both hands over his mouth.

**Pell Orsund** 
Ivo?

**Mo Itaya** 
Ivo, what happened?
He took his hands away. His face was wet.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
I was saying 'glad' and I thought of the other stool at my bench. I have been setting out two cups for three days and I could not see who sits on it.

**Mo Itaya** 
Bench Four. The roster says Dembe Okoro.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Dembe.

**Imre Hale** 
Nobody here can see their faces. Everybody here thought of someone.

**Illuminara** 
Ivo. When you cannot see her face, say the word anyway. Say it as a thing you owe her. It does not need to be a good word. It needs to be on time.

Four minutes by the clock on the wall. Nobody left the Hall. Hale stood with her hand on the lever and her eyes shut, and Illuminara said nothing, because the lever was Hale's and nothing she said in those four minutes would be worth the trust she had been lent. At the fifth minute Hale opened her eyes and put the lever back herself.
The aperture woke. Pell began again. Ivo said his word in time.

They ran three more cycles, clean. The burn trace, which had climbed all night, lay flat as a table. On the fourth cycle the Trine answered with something that the rig turned into a word and Pell, after a pause, translated himself.

**Pell Orsund** 
It says 'again.'
The board showed thirty-one greens through three whole cycles, and no one in the Hall drew breath until Mo said, quite calmly, from the middle of the list:

**Mo Itaya** 
Tamsin Wray. My deputy. I could not hold her for an hour. I had her name on a list and I thought it was a stranger's. She is a tall woman. She laughs through her nose. I have her.

**Pell Orsund** 
Hers was the badge that blinked.

**Imre Hale** 
And the nine? If she can come back, why can they not?

**Illuminara** 
I do not know. My guess is that the fold reached her before the tidy had finished with her, and the nine it finished. I would like to be wrong, and I will not tell you that I am.
Hale said nothing, and did not take her hand from the lever, and Illuminara understood that this too was an answer, and a fair one.

scenes.title: Two Twos
paragraphs: *Aperture Hall · 12:55, two hours forty-five before failure by the old clock*

Pell's rival had a sequel. He had been quiet for an hour, and then he put two sheets side by side on the bench, Mo's ledger page with its nine minutes and a printout of the burn trace, the numbers circled.

**Pell Orsund** 
Nine stops. Nine jumps in the burn, each at the minute Mo wrote down. The tidy was what was spending the lattice. Every time they cleared someone, it cost. Since the badges went onto the beat, nobody has been cleared and the line has not moved. Re-fitted at this load, it has not nine hours in it but a hundred and forty hours of contact.

**Imre Hale** 
Say that again.

**Pell Orsund** 
You can check it against her minutes yourself.
Hale took the sheets and checked, and checked again, and then folded the printout into her pocket. Illuminara stood at the lens, aware that the next thing would have to be asked and not given.

**Illuminara** 
Trine. May I tell you something about the sea?

**The Trine** 
We are listening with three.

**Illuminara** 
You said the sea is more than three, and you are afraid of it. I think you are right to be afraid. I do not want to teach you to see more all at once. That is the flood. I think you can hold more without holding more at the same time.

**The Trine** 
How? Three is three. More is murmur.

**Illuminara** 
Show me two.
Pell sent two tones. The lens held them, and gave them back, and the Trine's quiet settled around the sound.

**Illuminara** 
Now two again. After a gap. Not three. Two, and a gap, and two.

He sent a pair, and the gap, and a pair. For a long moment the lens did nothing at all. Illuminara gripped the bench hard enough that the washers rattled in their saucer. This was where the tidy would begin if it was going to.

**The Trine** 
Two. And another two. The first two is a two, and the second is a two. That is two things. Two things! That is not more than three. It is two of two.

**Illuminara** 
Yes. Two of two.

**The Trine** 
It is a name. We will call it twotwo. Twotwo, twotwo!

The three tones came up together and wide, and something went through the Hall that Illuminara had no word for in any of her languages. Hale's hand was still on the lever. She had not taken it off. She had also not pulled it.

**The Trine** 
Is the sea made of two of two? Is the sea made of the clear?

**Illuminara** 
I think it may be. You can look inside a group when you choose, one at a time. You do not have to look at any of it. This is yours to decide.

**The Trine** 
We would like to look. Slowly. Do not let us look at all of it.

**Illuminara** 
Then we will go slowly, and I will tell you if I do not know. There is something else, and I would like Mo to say it.
Mo came to the edge of the field with the ledger open in both hands. When she began, her voice was level in the way a plank is level over a gap.

**Mo Itaya** 
Dembe Okoro.

**The Trine** 
Dembe Okoro. One.

**Mo Itaya** 
Corin Aldous.

**The Trine** 
One. Another one.
She read nine names. She did not know the faces. She read them one at a time, each one a one, and the Trine took each as if it were being given a sealed thing and told not to open it.

**The Trine** 
Those are ones. We cleared ones. We did not know murmur was made of ones.

**Illuminara** 
I do not know where they are. I will not tell you that I do.

**The Trine** 
Neither do we. We cannot count what we let go, but now we have twotwo, and we could start.

**Imre Hale** 
Not today.
Hale had come out from beside the lever. She stood next to Illuminara and looked at the lens for the first time without any weapon in the look.

**Imre Hale** 
Not today, and not on a clock I did not set. If the Contact Office agrees, and the lattice holds a hundred and forty hours, then once a week, for one hour, with the nine names said at the start of every meeting. And when I pull the lever, it is not a murmur. You will hear a count that goes down. Three, two, one, and then quiet. That quiet is me.

**The Trine** 
Three, two, one, quiet. Quiet is you. We will learn the nine as nine ones, one at a time. It may take us all of the first meeting.

**Imre Hale** 
Then it takes the first meeting.
Ivo Petrenko had come in behind Mo and stood by the door, and now he spoke without being asked.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Bench Four has two stools. If they can hold her name as a one, can they hold her ping? Her badge is in the locker. I know the hook. I know the second it used to ping on, because I have been waiting for it for three days without knowing what I was waiting for.

**Imre Hale** 
That is a fourth thing on the cable.

**Illuminara** 
Not if the relay and the roll stay silent that hour. The hum with the thirty-one, and her one ping. Two things, and well within three.

**Imre Hale** 
Then here is what I will accept. Next hour, not today. Her badge on its own second, Ivo holding it, and the Trine looking for one thing with that pulse and nothing else. A blink on my board or a jump on Pell's trace, and I count down and close. If they find nothing, we stop at the hour and try the next name in a week.

**The Trine** 
One thing with that pulse. We are afraid. We would like to look.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
So would I.

scenes.title: Nine Plates
paragraphs: *Aperture Hall · seven days later, the next weekly hour*

The first hour had gone the way the Director's schedule said, and the Trine had come out of it knowing four of the nine names as two twos. Today the relay and the roll stood silent, only the hum went down the cable, and Ivo Petrenko stood in the near field with a badge on a lanyard, holding it as if it were warm.

**Pell Orsund** 
Trace is flat. Board is green. All thirty-one.

**Imre Hale** 
Then go.
Ivo pressed the clip. The badge pinged on its own second, a little off the beat, a small dry click that nobody in the Hall had heard in days.

**The Trine** 
One. A one with its own time. It is not in the hum. Is it the one?

**Ivo Petrenko** 
It was hers. It goes on the second beat of the third bar. I hung it up myself.

**The Trine** 
We are looking. It is smaller than afraid. We are looking.
For forty seconds nothing happened. Then the lens held a tone that was not the ping. It was one tone, faint and slow, a third of a beat behind where the badge had been.

**Pell Orsund** 
That is not her. I cannot tell you what that is. It could be an echo of the clip on the loop.

**Illuminara** 
It could. It could be something that kept her time and has been keeping it since the fourth.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Do it again.

He pressed it again, and the faint tone came a third of a beat late again, and it did not come on the second press unless the first had been sent. Nothing blinked on the board. The trace did not move.

**The Trine** 
One. A one in the sea, with a late time. We do not know what it is made of. It is very small. We did not tidy it.

Hale closed the hour herself, and she did it the way she had promised. *Three, two, one,* came out of the rig in her flat voice, and then quiet, and the Trine's answer was one low tone that Pell, without being asked, did not translate.
*Lantern Station, mess hall · the same evening, 18:10*

The table had forty settings on it. Thirty-one people sat at it, eating a stew that had been argued over for an hour and was better for it. Mo Itaya was laying the last place, Bench Four's place, and Ivo had put a lanyard beside the plate, hooked over the fork, where a person would hang a coat.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
She is not back. I know that. Something kept her time for forty seconds, a third of a beat late, and I do not know what it was.

**Illuminara** 
Neither do I. It is one pulse, and it is more than we had a week ago.

**Mo Itaya** 
Draw thirty-one. Set forty. That is what the Director decided, and I think she is right, though I could not tell you why. Now I think I could.
Hale had come in last. She did not sit at the head of the table. She stood behind an empty chair among the thirty-one, listening to Pell tell a story that she had already heard.

**Imre Hale** 
I still think I was right to hold the shutter.

**Illuminara** 
You were. It is the reason anyone could stand there.

**Imre Hale** 
And I would pull it again tonight, on a blink. I do not know what a person does with being right in a room with nine plates.

Illuminara did not answer. It was not hers to answer, and she knew the sound of a room where something had been mended and something else had not. Mo Itaya crossed to the empty chair with a clean plate and set it down in front of the Director, squarely, the way she set every plate.

**Mo Itaya** 
I cannot forgive you for the shutter. I am not sure there is anything to forgive, and if there is, it is not mine to give. The nine would have to say it, and they cannot. This is what I can do. Sit. That plate is from me.
Hale looked at the plate for a long moment. Then she sat, among the thirty-one, and Pell, without a pause in his story, passed her the bread.

Afterwards Ivo walked Illuminara to the tender's bay. At the dock the speaker by the hatch gave one small click, and a very faint voice, three tones in a rising chord, that the rig had not been told to translate. They stood and listened until it stopped.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Same again next week?

**Illuminara** 
Same again.

critic_line: Illuminara helps the Trine understand what their lens is doing, then protects three voluntary ways of standing while Hale keeps the shutter; thirty-one people remain present, the nine are neither erased nor falsely restored, and Mo—not Illuminara—sets the final plate without pretending that forgiveness has been earned.

translation_sl.title: VESOLJE, KI JE ZNALO ŠTETI LE DO TRI
translation_sl.deck: Enaintrideset ljudi na raziskovalni postaji drug za drugim bledi iz spomina sosednjega vesolja, ki ne more hkrati obdržati več kot treh stvari; ko je do odpovedi odprtine še devet ur in direktorica drži roko nad zaklopom, Illuminara prebere skladiščno knjigo, preizkusi dve teoriji z dvanajstimi podložkami in nežnemu ljudstvu pomaga šteti po dve dvojici, ne da bi od kogar koli zahtevala, naj se vidi kot manj, kot je.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v enem dnevu in teden pozneje: miza, pogrnjena za štirideset, direktorica, ki hoče okno zapreti, dvanajst podložk in kabel, ki prenaša dež, trije načini navzočnosti in ura, nastavljena na en utrip, zaklop, zaprt za štiri minute, štetje dveh dvojic in prvi preizkus za devet imen ter krožnik, postavljen na prazno mesto.

scenes.title: Miza, pogrnjena za štirideset
paragraphs: *Postaja Lantern, jedilnica · 06.40, devet ur pred odpovedjo mreže*

Mo Itaya je dolgo mizo znova pogrnila za štirideset in za devetimi mesti spet ni bilo nikogar. To je storila brez odločitve, kakor roka najde stikalo v hiši, v kateri je živela leta, in stala je nad priborom s knjigo, pritisnjeno ob rebra, ko je Illuminara stopila skozi loputo.

**Mo Itaya** 
Prevzetih štirideset obrokov, pojedenih enaintrideset. Tako je pri vsakem obroku, odkar se je odprlo okno. Ne morem vam povedati, kdo je teh devet, moje roke pa vedo. Kar naprej segajo po dodatnih krožnikih.

**Illuminara** 
Potem so vaše roke najboljša priča na postaji. Kaj pravi papir?

**Mo Itaya** 
Papir ne pozablja. V knjigi je štirideset imen. V omaricah je štirideset značk, enaintrideset pa jih visi na trakovih. Značka zapiska vsakih devetdeset sekund do dne, ko neha, in devet jih je nehalo. Nikoli ne piskajo skupaj. Vsaka ima svojo sekundo, kakor dež na strehi.

Ob vsakem imenu v knjigi je Mo zapisala minuto, ko se je piskanje končalo, s skrbno pisavo ženske, ki prepisuje besede iz jezika, ki ga ne zna več brati. Illuminara je prvi dve imeni tiho prebrala na glas. *Dembe Okoro. Corin Aldous.*

**Illuminara** 
Vam kaj pomenita?

**Mo Itaya** 
Imeni sta. Vem, da sta imeni. Kakor če bi me kdo vprašal po pomenu besede v jeziku, ki sem ga nekoč govorila.
Direktorica Lanterna ni bila velika ženska in mirovala je kakor nekdo, ki je drugi dan nehal spati in namesto tega začel šteti. Vstopila je brez trkanja in ni sedla.

**Imre Hale** 
Vi ste svetovalka za stik. Rekli so mi, da znate prebrati sobo v jeziku, ki ga nima. Ne potrebujem branja sobe. Potrebujem nekoga, ki mi bo povedal, da se ne motim, ker hočem stikalo.

**Illuminara** 
Kaj stikalo naredi?

**Imre Hale** 
Konča vse. Mreža bo odprtino držala še devet ur, nato bo pregorela, nove pa v moji karieri ne bo zgradil nihče. Končam lahko v devetih sekundah. Pell pravi, da je druga stran nežna, in verjamem mu; slišala sem jo. Opravičuje se. Opravičuje se kakor čistilec, ki je z vrat izbrisal ime. Nežnost, ki briše moje ljudi, je orožje z lepimi manirami, in rada bi jo zaprla.

**Illuminara** 
To je resen ugovor in ni neumen.

**Imre Hale** 
Nisem vas prosila za mnenje o svojem ugovoru.

**Illuminara** 
Ne. Vseeno vam ga povem, ker mislim, da nočete svetovalke, ki se vas boji. Prosim vas, naj zaklop ostane vaš in naj ga uporabite v trenutku, ko značka utihne. Ne po moji ali Pellovi presoji. Po pisku.

**Imre Hale** 
In če bi ga raje uporabila zdaj?

**Illuminara** 
Potem ga lahko uporabite in jaz bom nosila posledico. Toda enaintrideset ljudi je še tu. Del teh devetih ur bi rada porabila za to, da ugotovimo, kaj je to pospravljanje, preden sklenemo, da je zgolj orožje.
Hale je pogledala mizo, devet mest in za trenutek ničesar.

**Imre Hale** 
Še eden utihne in zaprem. Brez prerekanja.

**Illuminara** 
Brez prerekanja.

**Imre Hale** 
Od četrtega izginotja so v dvorani največ trije ljudje naenkrat. Nič ni pomagalo. Kar izginjali so.

Illuminara je obrnila knjigo proti svetlobi. Devet prekinitev v dveh dneh in nobena ni bila povezana s tem, kdo je stal pred odprtino. Leta je bila sodna tolmačka in se učila, da je enota pomena tisto, kar poslušalec lahko obdrži, nikoli pa še ni srečala poslušalca, čigar meja bi bila zapisana v skladiščni knjigi.

**Illuminara** 
Če je bila dvorana skoraj prazna, ljudje pa so še vedno izginjali, potem ne šteje ljudi v dvorani. Pomika se po seznamu.

**Imre Hale** 
Seznamu česa?

**Illuminara** 
Vsega, kar je razglasila za šum. Rada bi vedela, kaj ima za šum in kaj od našega poleg nas še doseže tisto lečo.

scenes.title: Šum
paragraphs: *Dvorana odprtine, Lantern · 07.20, osem ur in dvajset minut pred odpovedjo*

Odprtina je stala sredi hladne bele sobe, leča v višini vrat, za katero ni bilo ničesar, svetlejša v sredini kakor ob robu. V steno ob okvirju je bil privit vzvod, dolg kakor moška podlaket, Hale pa je stala z roko dva centimetra od njega.
Pell Orsund je imel slušalke potisnjene nazaj in na mizi napravo iz žic, ki je tone spreminjala v besede, ter opravičujoče vedenje nekoga, ki že dva dni tolmači nečemu, česar ne more videti.

**Pell Orsund** 
Naprava jim dodeli najbližjo našo besedo, najbližja pa ni vedno blizu. Priključena je na postajno zanko, isti kabel, po katerem teče mreža, zato lahko leča sliši vse, kar nosi zanka. Nikoli niso poslali več kot treh tonov. Mislil sem, da so plahi. Merilnik obremenitve je od odprtja okna devetkrat poskočil. Pripisal sem to segrevanju odprtine.

**Illuminara** 
Smem govoriti z njimi sama? Samo vi in jaz v dvorani.

**Imre Hale** 
O samoti odloča direktorica, direktorica pa ostaja.

**Illuminara** 
Potem trije, eden pa zunaj polja. Kaže, da je to njihovo število.
Hale se je skoraj nasmehnila, kar je bilo na njenem obrazu videti kakor bolečina. Illuminara je stopila pred lečo in Pella prosila za en sam ton. Odprtina je odgovorila z enim.

**Trine** 
Ena.
Nato dva in odgovorila sta dva. Nato trije in trije, ki so se vrnili, so bili zgoraj svetli in razcefrani, kakor nekdo, ki se zasmeji, preden se za to odloči.

**Trine** 
Tri! Tri, tri. Dobrodošli v jasnem. Mi smo Trine, kar smo trije, in mi trije smo eno, in tako se štejemo, da ne izgubimo števila. Prihajate v enicah. To je prijazno. Še nič ni prišlo v enicah.

**Illuminara** 
Kaj pa je prišlo?

**Trine** 
Šum. Zelo veliko šuma, pa smo ga pospravili, ker pospravljamo. Oprostite, če je bil vaš. Šum je vse, česar je več kot tri. Ni slab. Je morje. Morja ne moremo držati, zato držimo jasno in morje spustimo. Ko je jasno polno šuma, nihče od nas ne razlikuje nas treh od nas treh. Nismo bili ranjeni. Nismo bili nič.
Illuminara je tedaj razumela, kako dolgo je bilo to ljudstvo prestrašeno in kako urejeno lahko postane ljudstvo, kadar ima njegov strah številko.

**Illuminara** 
Kam gre šum, ko ga pospravite? Kaj je v morju?

**Trine** 
Nazaj v morje. Ne gledamo. Ne moremo ga prešteti.

**Illuminara** 
Hvala, ker ste mi povedali, da ne morete pogledati. To je najbolj koristna stvar, ki jo je danes kdo rekel. Zdaj vam moram nekaj povedati in rada bi povedala počasi. Šum so bili ljudje. V tem kraju nas je bilo štirideset, zdaj nas je enaintrideset.

**Trine** 
Ljudje. Enice. Veliko enic? Ne razumemo enic, ki jih je veliko. Trije vas slišimo in mi trije ne razumemo.

**Illuminara** 
Vem. Ne prosim vas, da nehate pospravljati. Mislim, da bi vas to ranilo. Prosim vas za čas, da poiščem nekaj drugega.

**Trine** 
Že dolgo smo si želeli nekaj novega. Novo je v šumu. Tega nismo vedeli.
Ton je zbledel. Hale ni premaknila roke in Illuminara je razumela, da ji direktorica daje prav to: dva centimetra zraka za delo.

**Imre Hale** 
Opravičilo kakor čistilec. Rekla sem in še enkrat bi rekla.

**Illuminara** 
Morda imate prav. Rada bi izvedela, kako zelo. Potrebujem pladenj, kamero, dvanajst enakih stvari in približno štirideset minut.

scenes.title: Dvanajst podložk
paragraphs: *Dvorana odprtine, delovna miza · 07.55, sedem ur in petinštirideset minut pred odpovedjo*

Pell je podložke našel v predalu pod spektrometrom, jeklene, široke kakor noht na palcu, in jih na pladenj štel tako skrbno kakor človek, ki deli karte. Illuminara je pladenj na palici potisnila v bližnje polje, da mimo okvirja ni segla ne roka ne rokav, kamero pa nastavila, naj šteje vsakih deset sekund.

**Pell Orsund** 
Imam nasprotno teorijo in všeč mi je. Poslušalca ni. Odprtina odteka vse, kar leži pred njo, naši ljudje so pesek v uri, naprava pa je v usta Trine položila 'oprostite', ker bi to rekli mi.

**Illuminara** 
Morda. Zato uporabljamo podložke. Če imate prav vi, jemlje stvari sorazmerno z njihovo količino. Če imajo prav Trine, jih jemlje sorazmerno s številom stvari, za katere misli, da so tam. Te napovedi se skoraj povsem razlikujeta.

Dvanajst podložk je raztresla po pladnju. Kamera je štiri minute štela dvanajst. Nato je ena med dvema posnetkoma izginila brez gibanja na sliki, kakor da je nikoli niso položili tja. Druga tri minute pozneje. Do petnajste minute so ostale tri podložke, za dlan narazen, tišina Trine pa je postala zadovoljna.

**Trine** 
Tri. Jasno. Jasno.

Pladenj je potegnila nazaj in nanj položila dvanajst novih podložk, tokrat v obroču, kjer so se robovi dotikali, v jeklenem krogu širine krožnička. Kamera jih je po desetih minutah štela dvanajst in po dvajsetih prav tako. Ton iz leče je bil skoraj nežen.

**Trine** 
Ena. Ena, narejena iz jasnega. Krog. Všeč nam je.

**Pell Orsund** 
Torej je pomembna razporeditev, ne količina. To je že proti meni.

**Illuminara** 
Še en poskus, da bova poštena do vas. Štiri medeninaste uteži: kilogram, petsto gramov, dvesto in sto. Če imate prav, težje izginejo prve.

Najprej je izginila stogramska utež. Po tridesetih minutah so na pladnju še vedno stale kilogramska, petstogramska in dvestogramska, tri stvari, toliko, kot je ostalo podložk. Najlažja je bila vzeta, najtežja je ostala.

**Pell Orsund** 
Umaknem plimo. Lepa plima je bila.

**Illuminara** 
Dobra nasprotna razlaga je bila, zato zaupam odgovoru. Leča ne šteje količine. Šteje tisto, kar drži čas samo s seboj.

**Pell Orsund** 
Torej podložke, ki se dotikajo, držijo čas in so ena, podložk, ki se ne dotikajo, pa je dvanajst. Poleg prvih treh, ki izstopajo, je vse drugo šum.
Ni več gledal pladnja. Gledal je ploščo zanke na steni, kjer je v sledi obremenitve sedelo devet majhnih konic kakor šivi.

**Pell Orsund** 
Drži čas samo s seboj. Kaj na tej postaji pa drži čas s čim? Značke. Enaintrideset značk, enaintrideset različnih sekund, vsakih devetdeset sekund, vse po istem kablu kakor mreža. To ni soba. To je dež.

**Imre Hale** 
Izpraznila sem dvorano.

**Pell Orsund** 
Izpraznili ste sobo. Piskanje sobe nikoli ni potrebovalo.
Hale se je odmaknila od vzvoda, tri korake, kakor da so jo potegnile podložke.

**Imre Hale** 
Potem jih povežite v obroč. Posadka naj se drži za roke in naj jih šteje kot eno.

**Illuminara** 
Ne.

**Imre Hale** 
Pri obroču je delovalo.

**Illuminara** 
Pri podložkah je delovalo. Obroč ljudi, ki se držijo, ker obiskovalec ne zna šteti, je nekaj, kar naredimo ljudem. Poleg tega Trine ne ponudi ničesar, kar bi lahko srečali, obroč pa je le zelo dober način pospravljanja.

**Imre Hale** 
Kaj potem?

**Illuminara** 
Trine lahko držijo tri stvari in vsako bodo držali, dokler drži čas samo s seboj. Naj bo zato vsaka od treh drugačne vrste: ena, ki se spreminja, ena, ki ostaja, ena, ki se vrača. In nihče ne bo stal v nobeni, če se s tem ne strinja. Natančno jim bom povedala, čemu služi in česa ne more obljubiti.

**Imre Hale** 
Enaintrideset ljudi boste prosili, naj stopijo pred stvar, ki jih je devet izbrisala.

**Illuminara** 
Prosila jih bom. Ne vem, kaj bodo rekli.

scenes.title: Trije načini navzočnosti
paragraphs: *Postaja Lantern, jedilnica · 09.25, šest ur in petnajst minut pred odpovedjo*
Prihajali so po dva ali tri, ker je to postala navada postaje, in sedali za dolgo mizo z devetimi praznimi mesti med njimi. Illuminara je stala na koncu, pred njo pa so bile podložke v krožničku.

Povedala jim je, kaj je odkrila, kakor bi povedala poroti, nato pa opisala tri vrste, v katere bi po njenem lahko sestavili množico. Stvar, ki se spreminja: en stavek, izgovorjen besedo za besedo, vsako z drugim glasom. Stvar, ki ostaja: en ton, ki ga mrmra toliko glasov, kolikor se jih odloči. Stvar, ki se vrača: seznam vseh imen na postaji, prebran na glas in nato znova, da bi lahko bil obdržan tudi vsak, ki ne želi nastopati — tako, da ga imenujejo.

**Illuminara** 
To so trije načini, da ste videni. Član posadke lahko izgovori besedo, mrmra ton ali je na seznamu. Vsako uro si lahko premislite. Če zavrnete vse tri, vam ne morem obljubiti, da boste obdržani, in ne bom se pretvarjala, da lahko.
Nekdo v ozadju je vprašal, ali morajo mrmrati uglašeno.

**Illuminara** 
V en glas. Ne v tonu.
Smeh je bil kratek in presenečen. Nato je Mo Itaya, ki ni sedla, knjigo zelo nežno položila na mizo, kakor da bi se lahko zbudila.

**Mo Itaya** 
Hočete, da se postavimo v vrsto in se pokažemo stvari, ki nas je devet izbrisala.

**Illuminara** 
Če se tako odločite, vam hočem dati način, da vas vidi. Nočem vam vzeti pravice, da jo sovražite.

**Mo Itaya** 
Ne sovraži nas. Tega ne morem odpustiti. Če bi nas sovražila, bi vedela, kaj naj naredim z rokami.
Nihče ni rekel ničesar. Hale je ob vznožju mize poslušala Mo, kakor človek posluša motor, ki je povedal resnico.

**Illuminara** 
Mo. Edini človek tukaj ste, ki je imel prav glede devetih, čeprav ne morete imenovati niti enega. Če bomo brali seznam, naj ga bere nekdo, ki ve, čemu seznam služi.
Mo je dolgo gledala knjigo.

**Mo Itaya** 
S štetjem se preživljam. Prebrala bom seznam. In še nekaj je, ker ima Pell prav glede dežja. Značka zapiska na sekundo, ko pritisnem sponko. Vsako pritisnem jaz. Piskanje ni neusklajeno zato, ker bi moralo biti.

**Illuminara** 
To lahko spremenite?

**Mo Itaya** 
Vseh enaintrideset lahko nastavim na utrip mrmranja. Zanka bi jih nosila kakor en ton. Nikogar ne stane ničesar razen nastavitve.

**Illuminara** 
Niso moje, da bi jih spreminjala, niti vaše. Ali koga moti značka na utrip?

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Moja lahko piska, kakor hoče.

Nekdo se je spet zasmejal. Ivo Petrenko, laboratorijski tehnik z mladeniškim obrazom in navado, da postavi dve skodelici, je rekel, da bo izgovoril besedo. Pell je rekel, da bo prevzel stavek, saj bi, če bi kdo izgubil nit, raje videl, da je to on.
Sedem ljudi je reklo, da bodo izgovorili besedo, petnajst, da bodo mrmrali, preostalih devet pa, da bodo imenovani. Direktorica je bila med deveterimi.

**Imre Hale** 
Direktorica, ki ukazuje zboru, je obroč z utripom. Stala bom ob vzvodu in bom ime.

**Illuminara** 
Potem je vzvod vaš in pravilo vaše. V trenutku, ko značka neha, pomežikne ali vam preprosto ni všeč, kar vidite, se zapre.

**Imre Hale** 
Tako bi ravnala v vsakem primeru.

**Illuminara** 
Vem. Hotela sem, da slišite, da to vem.

scenes.title: Štiri minute
paragraphs: *Dvorana odprtine · 10.35, pet ur pred odpovedjo*

Nastavljanje trakov je trajalo štirideset minut; Illuminara in Mo sta hodili od mize do mize z ročno uro ter vsako sponko pritisnili na utrip mrmranja, medtem ko je njen lastnik gledal. Štafeta je bila preprost stavek, ker je Trine lahko obdržal preprostost: *Tukaj smo, vsi, in zelo smo veseli, da ste tam.* Štirinajst besed, po dve za vsakega. Pell je vzel prvi dve, glas se mu je rahlo tresel, naslednji dve je izgovorila ženska, ki je šest let vodila prezračevanje in še nikoli ni govorila steni svetlobe, šesti par, *veseli, da*, pa je pripadel Ivu Petrenku.

Mrmranje je prihajalo iz postajne zanke, petnajst glasov in enaintrideset piskov, zloženih v en ton v stenah in tleh. Mo je stala ob robu polja s seznamom in na vrhu začela z ravnim, jasnim glasom. *Imre Hale. Odalys Brandt. Pell Orsund.* Brez premora je prebrala enaintrideset imen in na vrhu začela znova.
Illuminara je stala ob vzvodu in gledala ploščo značk na skrajni steni: enaintrideset majhnih lučk je utripalo tiho zeleno v ritmu. Odprtina se je nekoliko razsvetlila. Odgovor Trine je bil zelo tih.

**Trine** 
Tri. Slišimo tri. Eno, ki se premika, eno, ki ostaja, eno, ki se vrača. Ne vemo, iz česa so. Zelo lepe so.

V drugem krogu je Ivo izgovoril *veseli* tiho in za polovico utripa prepozno, mrmranje v zanki pa je potrebovalo en utrip, da ga je slišalo, in naslednjega, da se je zravnalo. V tem enem vdihu je bila na kablu četrta stvar. Lučka na plošči je ugasnila in se devet sekund pozneje spet prižgala, Illuminara pa je v kotu vida začutila trzaj leče kakor roko, ki začenja segati.
Hale je potegnila vzvod.
Zaklop se je zaprl z zvokom zadržanega diha, ki se sprosti. V nenadoma navadni sobi je mrmranje v stenah utihnilo, bela svetloba odprtine pa se je skrčila na kovanec in izginila.

**Imre Hale** 
Mežik je prekinitev. Tako je bilo pravilo.

**Illuminara** 
Tako je bilo pravilo. Imeli ste prav.
Ivo je stal z obema rokama čez usta.

**Pell Orsund** 
Ivo?

**Mo Itaya** 
Ivo, kaj se je zgodilo?
Odmaknil je roke. Obraz je imel moker.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Govoril sem 'veseli' in pomislil na drugi stol ob svoji mizi. Že tri dni postavljam dve skodelici in nisem mogel videti, kdo sedi na njem.

**Mo Itaya** 
Miza štiri. Na seznamu je Dembe Okoro.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Dembe.

**Imre Hale** 
Nihče tukaj ne vidi njihovih obrazov. Vsi tukaj so pomislili na nekoga.

**Illuminara** 
Ivo. Ko ne moreš videti njenega obraza, vseeno izgovori besedo. Izgovori jo kakor nekaj, kar ji dolguješ. Ni treba, da je dobra beseda. Pravočasna mora biti.

Štiri minute po uri na steni. Nihče ni zapustil dvorane. Hale je stala z roko na vzvodu in zaprtimi očmi, Illuminara pa ni rekla ničesar, ker je bil vzvod Halin in nič, kar bi v teh štirih minutah rekla, ne bi bilo vredno zaupanja, ki ji ga je Hale posodila. V peti minuti je Hale odprla oči in sama vrnila vzvod.
Odprtina se je prebudila. Pell je začel znova. Ivo je pravočasno izgovoril svojo besedo.

Opravili so še tri čiste kroge. Sled obremenitve, ki je rasla vso noč, je ležala ravna kakor miza. V četrtem krogu je Trine odgovoril z nečim, kar je naprava spremenila v besedo, Pell pa je po premoru sam prevedel.

**Pell Orsund** 
Pravi 'spet'.
Plošča je tri cele kroge kazala enaintrideset zelenih lučk in nihče v dvorani ni vdihnil, dokler ni Mo sredi seznama povsem mirno rekla:

**Mo Itaya** 
Tamsin Wray. Moja namestnica. Eno uro je nisem mogla obdržati. Njeno ime sem imela na seznamu in mislila sem, da je ime tujke. Visoka ženska je. Smeje se skozi nos. Imam jo.

**Pell Orsund** 
Njena značka je pomežiknila.

**Imre Hale** 
Kaj pa devet? Če se ona lahko vrne, zakaj se oni ne morejo?

**Illuminara** 
Ne vem. Ugibam, da jo je pregib dosegel, preden jo je pospravljanje dokončalo, devet pa je dokončalo. Rada bi se motila in ne bom vam rekla, da se.
Hale ni rekla ničesar in ni odmaknila roke od vzvoda, Illuminara pa je razumela, da je tudi to odgovor, in pošten.

scenes.title: Dve dvojici
paragraphs: *Dvorana odprtine · 12.55, po stari uri dve uri in petinštirideset minut pred odpovedjo*

Pellova nasprotna teorija je dobila nadaljevanje. Eno uro je molčal, nato je na delovno mizo položil dva lista, drug ob drugega: stran iz Mojine knjige z devetimi minutami in izpis sledi obremenitve, številke pa obkrožil.

**Pell Orsund** 
Devet prekinitev. Devet skokov obremenitve, vsak v minuti, ki jo je zapisala Mo. Pospravljanje je porabljalo mrežo. Vsakič, ko so koga počistili, je stalo. Odkar so značke v ritmu, ni bil očiščen nihče in črta se ni premaknila. Pri tej obremenitvi mreži ne ostaja devet ur, temveč sto štirideset ur stika.

**Imre Hale** 
Povejte še enkrat.

**Pell Orsund** 
Sami lahko preverite z njenimi minutami.
Hale je vzela lista, preverila in še enkrat preverila, nato pa izpis prepognila in spravila v žep. Illuminara je stala pri leči in vedela, da bo naslednjo stvar treba prositi, ne dati.

**Illuminara** 
Trine. Vam smem nekaj povedati o morju?

**Trine** 
Poslušamo s tremi.

**Illuminara** 
Rekli ste, da je morje več kot tri in da se ga bojite. Mislim, da se ga upravičeno bojite. Nočem vas naučiti videti več naenkrat. To bi bila poplava. Mislim, da lahko obdržite več, ne da bi hkrati držali več.

**Trine** 
Kako? Tri so tri. Več je šum.

**Illuminara** 
Pokažite mi dve.
Pell je poslal dva tona. Leča ju je zadržala in vrnila, tišina Trine pa se je naselila okoli zvoka.

**Illuminara** 
Zdaj še enkrat dve. Po premoru. Ne tri. Dve, premor in dve.
Poslal je par, premor in par. Leča dolgo ni naredila ničesar. Illuminara je tako močno stisnila delovno mizo, da so podložke zaropotale v krožničku. Če se bo pospravljanje začelo, se bo tu.

**Trine** 
Dve. In še dve. Prvi dve sta ena dvojica in drugi dve sta ena dvojica. To sta dve stvari. Dve stvari! To ni več kot tri. To sta dve od dveh.

**Illuminara** 
Da. Dve od dveh.

**Trine** 
To je ime. Rekli bomo dvadva. Dvadva, dvadva!

Trije toni so se dvignili skupaj in široko in skozi dvorano je šlo nekaj, za kar Illuminara ni imela besede v nobenem svojih jezikov. Halina roka je bila še na vzvodu. Ni je odmaknila. Tudi potegnila ga ni.

**Trine** 
Je morje narejeno iz dveh od dveh? Je morje narejeno iz jasnega?

**Illuminara** 
Mislim, da morda je. Ko se odločite, lahko pogledate v skupino, eno po eno. Ni vam treba pogledati ničesar. To je vaša odločitev.

**Trine** 
Radi bi pogledali. Počasi. Ne dovolite nam pogledati vsega.

**Illuminara** 
Potem bomo šli počasi in povedala vam bom, kadar ne bom vedela. Še nekaj je in rada bi, da to pove Mo.
Mo je stopila na rob polja z odprto knjigo v obeh rokah. Ko je začela, je bil njen glas raven kakor deska čez vrzel.

**Mo Itaya** 
Dembe Okoro.

**Trine** 
Dembe Okoro. Ena.

**Mo Itaya** 
Corin Aldous.

**Trine** 
Ena. Še ena.
Prebrala je devet imen. Obrazov ni poznala. Brala jih je enega za drugim, vsak je bil ena, Trine pa so vsakega vzeli, kakor da jim izročajo zapečateno stvar z navodilom, naj je ne odprejo.

**Trine** 
To so enice. Očistili smo enice. Nismo vedeli, da je šum narejen iz enic.

**Illuminara** 
Ne vem, kje so. Ne bom vam rekla, da vem.

**Trine** 
Tudi mi ne vemo. Ne moremo prešteti tistega, kar smo izpustili, toda zdaj imamo dvadva in lahko bi začeli.

**Imre Hale** 
Ne danes.
Hale je stopila izza vzvoda. Postavila se je ob Illuminari in prvič pogledala lečo brez orožja v pogledu.

**Imre Hale** 
Ne danes in ne po uri, ki je nisem nastavila jaz. Če se Urad za stike strinja in mreža zdrži sto štirideset ur, potem enkrat na teden po eno uro, z devetimi imeni, izgovorjenimi na začetku vsakega srečanja. Ko potegnem vzvod, to ni šum. Slišali boste odštevanje. Tri, dve, ena in nato tišina. Ta tišina sem jaz.

**Trine** 
Tri, dve, ena, tišina. Tišina ste vi. Devet se bomo naučili kot devet enic, eno za drugo. Morda bomo za to potrebovali vse prvo srečanje.

**Imre Hale** 
Potem bo trajalo vse prvo srečanje.
Ivo Petrenko je prišel za Mo in stal ob vratih, zdaj pa je spregovoril, ne da bi ga kdo prosil.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Pri mizi štiri sta dva stola. Če lahko njeno ime držijo kot eno, lahko držijo tudi njen pisk? Njena značka je v omarici. Poznam kljuko. Poznam sekundo, na katero je nekoč piskala, ker jo že tri dni čakam, ne da bi vedel, kaj čakam.

**Imre Hale** 
To je četrta stvar na kablu.

**Illuminara** 
Ne, če štafeta in seznam tisto uro molčita. Mrmranje z enaintridesetimi in njen en pisk. Dve stvari, varno znotraj treh.

**Imre Hale** 
Potem sprejmem naslednje. Naslednjo uro, ne danes. Njena značka na svoji sekundi, Ivo jo drži, Trine pa iščejo eno stvar s tem utripom in nič drugega. Mežik na moji plošči ali skok na Pellovi sledi in odštejem ter zaprem. Če ne najdejo ničesar, ob koncu ure nehamo in čez teden poskusimo z naslednjim imenom.

**Trine** 
Ena stvar s tem utripom. Strah nas je. Radi bi pogledali.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Tudi jaz.

scenes.title: Devet krožnikov
paragraphs: *Dvorana odprtine · sedem dni pozneje, naslednja tedenska ura*

Prva ura je potekala po direktoričinem urniku in Trine so jo končali tako, da so štiri od devetih imen poznali kot dve dvojici. Danes sta štafeta in seznam molčala, po kablu je šlo le mrmranje, Ivo Petrenko pa je stal v bližnjem polju z značko na traku in jo držal, kakor da je topla.

**Pell Orsund** 
Sled je ravna. Plošča je zelena. Vseh enaintrideset.

**Imre Hale** 
Potem začnite.
Ivo je pritisnil sponko. Značka je zapiskala na svoji sekundi, nekoliko izven ritma, majhen suh klik, ki ga v dvorani že več dni ni slišal nihče.

**Trine** 
Ena. Ena s svojim časom. Ni v mrmranju. Je to tista?

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Bila je njena. Oglasi se na drugem udarcu tretjega takta. Sam sem jo obesil.

**Trine** 
Gledamo. Manjše je od strahu. Gledamo.
Štirideset sekund se ni zgodilo nič. Nato je leča zadržala ton, ki ni bil pisk. En ton, šibek in počasen, za tretjino utripa za mestom, kjer je bila značka.

**Pell Orsund** 
To ni ona. Ne morem vam povedati, kaj je. Lahko je odmev sponke v zanki.

**Illuminara** 
Lahko. Lahko je nekaj, kar je držalo njen čas in ga drži od četrtega dne.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Še enkrat.
Znova je pritisnil in šibki ton je bil spet za tretjino utripa pozen, ob drugem pritisku pa ga ni bilo, če prej ni poslal prvega. Na plošči ni pomežiknilo nič. Sled se ni premaknila.

**Trine** 
Ena. Ena v morju, s poznim časom. Ne vemo, iz česa je. Zelo majhna je. Nismo je pospravili.

Hale je sama končala uro in to storila, kakor je obljubila. *Tri, dve, ena,* je iz naprave prišlo z njenim ravnim glasom, nato tišina, odgovor Trine pa je bil en nizek ton, ki ga Pell brez prošnje ni prevedel.
*Postaja Lantern, jedilnica · istega večera, 18.10*

Na mizi je bilo štirideset pogrinjkov. Za njo je sedelo enaintrideset ljudi in jedlo enolončnico, o kateri so se eno uro prepirali in je bila zato boljša. Mo Itaya je pogrinjala zadnje mesto, mesto pri mizi štiri, Ivo pa je ob krožnik položil trak in ga zataknil čez vilice, kamor bi človek obesil plašč.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Ni se vrnila. To vem. Nekaj je držalo njen čas štirideset sekund, za tretjino utripa pozno, in ne vem, kaj je bilo.

**Illuminara** 
Tudi jaz ne. En utrip je in to je več, kot smo imeli pred tednom.

**Mo Itaya** 
Prevzemi enaintrideset. Pogrni za štirideset. Tako je odločila direktorica in mislim, da ima prav, čeprav vam ne bi znala povedati, zakaj. Zdaj mislim, da bi.
Hale je prišla zadnja. Ni sedla na čelo mize. Stala je za praznim stolom med enaintridesetimi in poslušala Pella, ki je pripovedoval zgodbo, ki jo je že slišala.

**Imre Hale** 
Še vedno mislim, da sem imela prav, ko sem držala zaklop.

**Illuminara** 
Imeli ste. Zato je sploh kdo lahko stal tam.

**Imre Hale** 
In nocoj bi ga ob mežiku spet potegnila. Ne vem, kaj človek naredi s tem, da ima prav v sobi z devetimi krožniki.

Illuminara ni odgovorila. Odgovor ni pripadal njej in poznala je zvok sobe, v kateri je bilo nekaj popravljeno, nekaj drugega pa ne. Mo Itaya je stopila k praznemu stolu s čistim krožnikom in ga postavila pred direktorico, naravnost, kakor je postavila vsak krožnik.

**Mo Itaya** 
Ne morem vam odpustiti zaklopa. Nisem prepričana, da je sploh kaj odpustiti, če pa je, ni moje, da dam. Devet bi moralo to reči, pa ne morejo. To lahko naredim. Sedite. Ta krožnik je od mene.
Hale je dolgo gledala krožnik. Nato je sedla med enaintrideset in Pell ji je, ne da bi prekinil zgodbo, podal kruh.

Pozneje je Ivo pospremil Illuminaro do pristana plovila. Ob doku je zvočnik pri loputi enkrat tiho kliknil in zaslišal se je zelo slaboten glas, trije toni v naraščajočem akordu, ki jih naprava ni bila naučena prevesti. Stala sta in poslušala, dokler ni utihnil.

**Ivo Petrenko** 
Naslednji teden enako?

**Illuminara** 
Naslednji teden enako.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara pomaga Trine razumeti, kaj počne njihova leča, nato pa zaščiti tri prostovoljne načine navzočnosti, medtem ko Hale ohrani zaklop; enaintrideset ljudi ostane navzočih, devet ni niti izbrisanih niti lažno vrnjenih, zadnji krožnik pa brez pretvarjanja, da je odpuščanje zasluženo, postavi Mo — ne Illuminara.
